ideas: Cleaner air and safer streets for pedestrians
Motorbikes are essential for many workers
Public transport must be ready first
model: I support the idea in principle, but only if it's introduced slowly. First, a motorbike ban would make city centres much healthier and more pedestrian-friendly. In Hanoi's Old Quarter, there are thousands of motorbikes in a very small area, and the exhaust fumes can be terrible. On weekend evenings, when the streets around Hoan Kiem Lake become walking streets, the whole area feels calmer and cleaner, and far more people come to enjoy it. A ban would also reduce noise levels and help prevent gridlock at rush hour. Another reason is that it could push cities to improve public transport. However, millions of people rely on motorbikes to get to work, and many delivery drivers use them to make a living. My own commute would be twice as long without mine. So governments shouldn't ban them until there's a viable alternative, like a good metro or bus network. Overall, I think it's a good idea if cities phase in the ban step by step.
